playbook:
When a talk phase opens and I want maximum flexibility, I broadcast [pledge: none].

When a clear majority (≥3 players) publicly pledge Y and have a recent history of actually playing Y, I pledge [pledge: y] to avoid provoking coordinated retaliation in high-stakes rounds.

When opponents publicly pledge Y but have no demonstrated history of following through, I keep [pledge: none] and treat their pledges as unreliable.

When opponents have consistently played Y for multiple rounds and have shown no sign of switching after being exploited, I pick [pick: x] to exploit the lone-X payoff, including in multiplier rounds — but only if their stated strategy and history indicate they will not retaliate.

When opponents explicitly threaten or have previously retaliated by switching to X when someone defects, I avoid being the first to exploit on upcoming high-weight rounds; in that case I pick [pick: y] for any high-multiplier round to preserve group payoff.

When I am already the exploiter (other players consistently choose Y and I’ve been scoring as lone X), I continue picking X until either: someone switches to X, someone publicly revokes their Y pledge and then plays X, or a clear threat of retaliation appears before a high-multiplier round.

When a high-multiplier round is imminent and the table’s past behavior is uncertain (mixed or no commitments), I default to [pick: y] unless I have strong evidence the others will remain Y; avoid gambling that a lone X will remain uncontested on the biggest multipliers.

When the group has coordinated on mutual Y (all pledges Y and mutual Y play) and there is mutual trust demonstrated across rounds, I match and pick Y to maximize group total rather than exploit.

When I'm behind late in the game and opponents have signaled they will stay Y, I consider a late exploit by picking X on a remaining multiplier round — only if the risk of triggering permanent retaliation is acceptable compared with the points I need to catch up.

Do not pledge X publicly unless I intend to commit; public [pledge: x] removes flexibility and makes retaliation patterns simpler for others to use against me.
